findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the multiple dish machines failing to meet sanitizing requirements:
1) The heat sanitizing restaurant dish machine reached 153F after four runs. The facility consulted their engineer to check the heat boosters. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/10 to verify that the machine is reaching a minimum heat sanitizing temperature of 160F.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The chemical sanitizing dish machine at the Globe was dispensing 0 ppm sanitizer. CORRECTED- the machine was primed multiple times and the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Chlorine. 
Dishes produced in the restaurant should must be brought to the main kitchen dish machine for proper ware washing until the machine is serviced. Ensure all dish machines are tested frequently to verify that the machine is reaching the sanitizing concentration (or a minimum temperature of 160F) as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a gallon of milk and creamer without date marking at the bar reach in cooler. CORRECTED- the PIC could not guarantee the date these items were opened, and discarded them as a result. Ensure that date marking happens within 24 hours of opening a TCS (time/temperature controlled for safety) food. To identify TCS foods, look for the phrases “refrigerate after opening” or “keep refrigerated” on the item packaging. Additionally, anything prepared in the kitchen that is not shelf-stable must also be date marked within 24 hours of preparation.

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed two areas to have soiled food-contact surfaces. Both areas were at the detached Globe Tavern. The first area is the drain-tube connected to the soda gun holder. The tube has a build-up of soils in the tube. A reusable straw brush could be a good tool for cleaning this. The second area is the ice scoop holder at the bar. The scoop holder has a build-up of soils along the bottom edges. The scoop comes directly into contact with these soils when the scoop is inserted in the holder. Ensure both of these areas are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. They also require regular sanitization, as they are a food-contact surface (ice and soda are both considered food).

Inspector will return 09/18/25 to re-inspect the condition of these areas.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Inspector observed the area inside of the ice machine to be soiled. Maintenance is currently cleaning inside of the ice machine. The violation is considered corrected on site. Protect all food from potential contamination 
(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: Upon arrival the conveyor dish machine had an alarm sign on the display and the final rinse temperature gauge was sitting at 120F. The dish washer noted that the booster heater had not been turned on. The booster was turned on and the final rinse temperature gauge came up to over 189F quickly. A maximum registering thermometer was run and the dish machine is now sanitizing at 158F. Ensure that staff are properly trained for the job they are performing. The violation was corrected on site. 
(A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: Inspector found 11 portions of ROP fish thawed in the 2 door cooler still in the packaging. Package read remove from packaging before thawing. The fish portions were discarded in the garbage. Thaw foods properly.

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: A drawer holding utensils at a the kitchen utensil storage area is soiled. The drawer was removed and drawer including all of the utensils was given to dish for cleaning. Maintain this area free of accumulated soil. 
(A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Two of the hand sinks in the kitchen are observed to be without a supply of disposable towels. Towels were added to the dispensers at the hand sinks. Keep hand sinks properly supplied so that they can be used for hand washing when needed. 
The violation is considered to be corrected on site.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

The dish machine at the bar tested at 0 ppm chlorine. The machine was subsequently found to be without sanitizer in the container. The container was replaced, the machine primed and cycles run until the chlorine residual tested at the required 50 ppm of chlorine. Ensure that the rack of glasses that was pulled from the machine this morning is run through the machine again to properly clean and sanitize them. Test the machine daily to verify that the machine is functioning properly. Train the bartenders to test the machine and notify someone if the machine is not working properly.  The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

A box of Boursin is observed in the prep line cooler on top of the wrapped quarter pans. This area is above the fill line and considered outside of refrigeration. The Boursin was 47F internally. The Boursin was discarded in the garbage. Also, a dish of fired arugula is observed to be sitting at room temperature on the prep line. Arugula is a vegetable and once cooked should be treated as a TCS food.  The arugula was discarded in the garbage. The violations are considered corrected on site. Take care to properly refrigerate temperature control for safety (TCS) foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Inspector observed wet wiping cloths laying on surfaces in many areas of the kitchen and dish room. When not in use wet wiping cloths shall be stored either in sanitizer or taken to the laundry. Develop the habit of properly handling wet wiping cloths.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Inspector observed the drawers at Bakery and the banquet prep to be soiled and holding clean utensils in them, Properly clean and sanitize drawers so that their soil does not contaminate the food contact surfaces of the clean utensils. Store utensils properly protected.

findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following physical facility repairs needed (no longer smooth, easily cleanable, non-absorbent):

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed multiple items within the nearest walk-in cooler to the main dish machine area to have items past the date marked date. Items included tapenade, lemon aioli, dressings, sour cream, and a few other sauces. Dates indicated disposition around 7/21 - well over the 7 day date marking system. Discussed with CFPM. CFPM voluntarily took items out of the walk-in cooler and discarded. Ensure staff is aware to periodically going through coolers and check date marking for expired foods. COS.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

Observed multiple spray bottles of lactic acid product to be too strong. Multiple attempts to test the lactic acid spray bottles yielded a concentration of 2258 ppm. Correct concentration range for lactic acid products should be 704-1875 ppm. Inspector demonstrated test strips use with spray bottle in front of CFPM. Facility did not have test strips for the lactic acid product and was not aware. The concentration in the bottles should be lower. Front house (bar and breakfast areas) are utilizing the lactic acid spray bottles. Back house (kitchen) is utilizing quaternary ammonium from the dispensers (test strips available). After discussion with PIC/CFPM/head chef, the facility will switch back over to quaternary ammonium buckets with rags for the front house. Facility was utilizing rags with the spray bottles from what it appeared. Spray bottles should have paper towel use as the rags cannot be immersed in sanitizer. PIC indicated this practice will cease. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

(REPEAT) Observed salmon to be thawing within the reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Instructions on the fish indicate to removed from packaging and thaw under refrigeration. This was discussed at the last inspection on 2/22/22. Practice has not ceased. Discussed with PIC/CFPM. He indicated he will reiterate to staff the proper thawing practice of ROP food (when indicated on package to remove before thawing). COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed fruit flies around the bar area (mainly near both hand sinks). Discussed not pouring sticky drinks (sodas, mixed alcoholic drinks) down the hand sinks to hinder the pest issue. Drain flies should be mitigated. Inspector will follow-up on 8/15/22.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas to be in need of repairs:
1. Missing tiles/coving by the main entrance door to the kitchen near larger dish machine area, as well as around the base pillar of the mop sink area/quat dispenser area. Re-tile area.
2. The metal coving near the 2 walk-in coolers/walk-in freezer is coming away in the front. Metal should be sealed to the wall.
3. The caulking at the main dish machine is coming away and molding (at the entrance of the dish machine area). Re-caulk area.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

Wait staff is not completely licensed. Discussed with PIC. All staff that handles food must have food handler's license. Ensure staff is licensed within 30 days of employment. 

Complaint valid. Ensure staff has licenses and copies in binder by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed both sani buckets in the kitchen to have 0 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Both dispensers in the kitchen were tested at 400 ppm - functioning. Ensure sani buckets are changed every 4 hours or so to keep concentration of sanitizer between 200-400 ppm. Test strips were available at the 3 compartment sink. Ensure use of test strips to verify. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed multiple areas where salmon was thawing in its reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Discussed with PIC that fish should be taken out of packaging prior to thawing in coolers. COS.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed employee health reporting agreements to be present but not signed. Ensure all food handling employees including dish washers and servers sign the document. Inspector will follow-up on 11/4/21.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

Observed the sanitization spray bottle to be too strong - over 200 ppm of bleach. Test strips bleached out after turning black. Discussed proper concentration of bleach with PIC. PIC corrected the bottle. Ensure test strip use to verify correct bleach concentration.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed all stacked plates at the breakfast area to not be protected from cross-contamination. Discussed various methods with PIC. Discussed flipping plates over, discussed storing plates in the cabinets before service, discussed taking away the top plate before each service. Discuss with breakfast staff to ensure a method that works for facility. Be sure staff is aware.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

(REPEAT) Observed walk-in freezer to have a severe accumulation of frost and ice. Discussed repairs with PIC. Janitor came to kitchen during inspection and said the only method they have to hinder frost accumulation is to regularly defrost the walk-in freezer. Ensure an appropriate repair service comes to the facility before the next routine inspection. The walk-in freezer has so much frost, there is no way to even recognize the food products covered in ice. The gasket/seal appears to be coming away from the door which may be the issue. Repair this seal/gasket. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 9/12/19 and 7/19/21.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no bleach test strips at the facility. Facility is utilizing bleach spray bottles. Ensure test strips are available. Inspector will follow-up on 11/4/21.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed mop to be drying within the sanitization bucket. Ensure mops are hung in a manner that allows to air and/or drip dry. Discussed with PIC. Same issue was noted during the last routine inspection, but within the general comments. COS.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the CFPM’s available at the facility to lack allergen training certification. Multiple food handler’s have the certification; however, the certified food protection manager’s are the only staff that need this certification. Ensure all CFPM’s have taken course and printed out copies to prove completion. Put copies into the public health binder.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed ice dumped in kitchen hand sink. Cease practice. Hand sinks are for hand washing only. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines. 

Observed kitchen hand sink near 3 compartment sink/prep area to not have hot water. Discussed repairs with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 7/29/21.

Observed bar dish machine to have 0-10 ppm of chlorine bleach. Dish machine is not dispensing sanitizer correctly. Discussed with PIC to call EcoLab. Inspector will follow-up on 7/21/21.

Both of these issues are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 9/12/19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

Observed no heat test strips and/or maximum registering thermometer available to measure temperature of the dish machine. Discussed purchasing testing device for a heated dish machine with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 7/29/21.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed duct tape on the handle of the reach-in freezer. Repair handle. Cease use of duct tape. Duct tape is not an approved material. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No CFMs present in facility. Adequate coverage is necessary for category I facilities. Ensure adequate coverage. Reference 750.540.
